architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: For both T = 120 C and T = 130 C, Delta_T must fall within the same one of these non-overlapping numerical bands: -46.1567% to -39.3567% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 13.8433% to 20.6433% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -76.1567% to -69.3567% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. Meeting this criterion provisionally accepts that formulation-level rule for the measured realization only; it is not robust formulation-level acceptance because the card lacks a contemporaneous matched E2 preparation and preparation repeats.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary 120 C and 130 C viscosities are measured directly in S1C41, so they do not depend on a rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family as the candidate and do not transfer the unmodified-family shared thermal shape. This direct sweep is admissible under the binding audit and establishes evidence only for the measured AC1920/TK100-modified chemistry and state range; it does not establish unrestricted future M-ANCHOR transferability or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Evaluate 120 C and 130 C separately. H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified for the measured realization if either Delta_120 or Delta_130 differs from -42.7567% by more than 3.40 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if either Delta_120 or Delta_130 is at or below -42.7567%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if either Delta_120 or Delta_130 is at or above -42.7567%. If the two temperatures imply different classifications, or no single prediction band contains both values, the three-rule formulation-level interpretation is not accepted and remains confounded by realization state.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT to quantify between-preparation displacement of the viscosity scale before making a formulation-level conclusion; subsequent hypothesis adjudication requires matched independent S1C41 and unmodified E2 preparations with separate 120 C and 130 C contrasts.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity at 120 C and 130 C from the 80-130 C sweep, evaluated separately as percentage changes relative to the unmodified E2 reactive-core reference: Delta_T = 100 * [eta_S1C41(T) / eta_E2(T) - 1] for T = 120 C and 130 C. The fitted E_eta is secondary and is only an apparent rheological temperature-response descriptor.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-SWEEP is an admissible direct measurement for the modified chemistry, belongs to the stable five-card top set, and uses the smallest modifier burden among the tied experiments while retaining wide numerical separation among the registered predictions. It is committed as a discriminating probe rather than a mitigation claim because the single-preparation protocol cannot resolve the documented realization variability, thermal-hold drift, or separate AC1920 from TK100 effects.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C41::M-SWEEP and use the Proposer's minimum-modifier-burden tie break among the five VOI-tied cards. I follow the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator, rather than the Proposer, on interpretation: the direct sweep is informative, but one preparation without a contemporaneous matched E2 comparator cannot support robust 3.40%-resolution formulation-level acceptance or modifier-specific attribution. Accordingly, all three registered hypotheses remain entangled with realization state even though the preregistered numerical predictions are separated.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: S1C41 uses 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100, within the stated supported intervention regions, but source-level external-prior queries returned no rows. Modifier functionality, recalculated NCO:OH, hot-hold behavior, and modifier-specific effects are unresolved.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The direct sweep removes reliance on unverified thermal-shape transfer and stays within the measured 80-130 C range. Remaining extrapolation concerns arise from moving from the unmodified reactive core to combined AC1920/TK100 chemistry and from generalizing one realization to the formulation.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The supplied 3.40% threshold is the residual of a shared-shape-plus-intercept fit, not a demonstrated between-preparation discrimination limit. Direct 120 C and 130 C readings avoid temperature extrapolation, but the card provides only one preparation.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High and potentially dominant: historical E2 preparations show max/min ratios of 3.57 at 120 C and 3.34 at 130 C, with sample CV values of 0.585 and 0.541. The selected card does not control this state uncertainty or provide a contemporaneous E2 denominator.

action_requests.reason: Introducing either modifier changes chemistry. This gate is required to determine whether one-point state calibration is defensible for that family or whether direct M-SWEEP verification is required.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local shared temperature-response regularity was measured primarily in the original E1-E3 reactive PUR chemistry family, with E2 as the reactive-core anchor; E1 +P is a separately identified chemical perturbation rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. A hypothesis-separating experiment must use a nonzero acrylic-like and/or minor-tackifier-like loading, so it would not automatically remain inside the chemistry support of the original regularity. The shared-shape shortcut therefore requires a chemistry-applicability audit; otherwise the candidate needs a direct 80-130 C sweep.
planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled realization-dependent viscosity level in the 120-130 C processing window, creating a risk that a nominal formulation will not reproducibly remain within its required processing-viscosity window.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: For nominally identical E2 realizations, viscosity at 120 C had a sample CV of 0.585 and a max/min ratio of 3.57; at 130 C the sample CV was 0.541 and the max/min ratio was 3.34. This measured spread establishes that formulation identity alone does not presently control the realized processing-temperature viscosity level.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response is covered by six-point 80-130 C sweeps for E1, E2, and E3, including multiple E2 realizations, whereas isothermal behavior is represented only by single 120 C hold runs for E1 and E5 with four observations from 15 to 90 min. No E2 hold trajectory is supplied, and there are no independent hold repeats. The two available trajectories also differ substantially: E1 changed by 9.51% from 15 to 60 min and 16.85% from 15 to 90 min, while E5 changed by 51.54% and 93.08%, respectively.
measurement_requirements: Use a modifier-containing candidate because the unmodified reactive core has no differential prediction and cannot separate H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC.
Measure viscosity directly at 120 and 130 C under a fully recorded, matched preparation and elapsed-time history; preserve the unknown source viscosity unit rather than inventing one.
Prefer an 80-130 C sweep in 10 C increments so the processing-window level and the candidate-specific temperature response are both measured rather than inferred across a chemistry change.
Pre-register the inert-dilution, associative-elevation, and plasticizing-depression predictions for the selected loading and classify the result using the applicable measurement-resolution threshold.

Use independent preparations sufficient to quantify realization spread, because the existing E2 spread of approximately 2.8-3.6-fold can overwhelm the 3.4% sweep or 8.8% anchor discrimination thresholds.

If residence-time stability is part of candidate admissibility, add a 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min with at least two independent repeats and report SI_15_60 separately from the initial viscosity level.
Do not use a single 110 C anchor to infer 120-130 C viscosity unless the audited chemistry-support assessment explicitly finds the shared thermal shape applicable to the selected candidate.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-core candidate containing a nonzero modifier loading, does the directly measured viscosity level at matched process state and 120-130 C agree with the inert-dilution prediction, exceed it beyond measurement resolution as predicted by acrylic-associative elevation, or fall below it as predicted by plasticizing-continuum depression?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is an AC1920/TK100-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. Therefore an M-ANCHOR reconstruction would be inadmissible under the binding audit. M-SWEEP is admissible because it directly measures the 120-130 C decision quantity and establishes the temperature-response shape for this modified chemistry rather than transferring the unmodified-family regularity.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: A measured 120-130 C level change within 3.40% of exactly one prediction identifies the supported formulation-level rule for S1C41: -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result at or below -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; a result at or above -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; and a departure from -42.76% exceeding 3.40% falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. No hypothesis is privileged in advance, so the result will be interpreted against all three preregistered falsification rules.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result not uniquely within 3.40% of one prediction would leave the three-rule model unresolved or indicate that none adequately describes this realization. Given the documented 2.8-3.6-fold E2 realization spread and the card's moderate process-state risk, such a result would also require considering uncontrolled preparation or elapsed-time state rather than assigning a modifier-level mechanism.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C within the 80-130 C sweep, reported as the level change relative to the unmodified reactive core; the sweep also yields the fitted apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: VOI-tied and equally discriminating, but its 17.5% acrylic loading imposes a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41 without adding hypothesis-pair separation.
VOI-tied and located at a directly supported 20% acrylic region, but exact proximity to an analogue anchor is not a ranking objective; it has greater modifier burden with no added discrimination.
VOI-tied and within the broad supported region, but its 22.5% acrylic loading is a larger departure from local chemistry without additional information value.

VOI-tied and externally supported at 25% acrylic, but it is the largest perturbation in the tied set and lies outside the conservative initial acrylic band while providing no extra hypothesis separation.

It separates the same three hypothesis pairs, but 7.5% TK100 lies 1.1 percentage points above the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4% cluster, producing nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score of 0.685208.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-SWEEP has the highest tied VOI score of 0.6875, separates all three pairwise comparisons among the registered level hypotheses, and measures the 120-130 C decision quantity directly rather than through an unverified shared-shape reconstruction. Its 15% acrylic and 5% tackifier loadings are both inside supported intervention regions. Among the tied cards, it follows the minimum-sufficient-intervention policy by using the lowest modifier burden. It does not resolve thermal-hold drift or preparation repeatability, which remain separate process-state uncertainties.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards separate all three registered hypothesis pairs, directly measure the processing-window level, remain within both externally supported modifier regions, and have identical VOI components. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden in the tied set: 15% AC1920 plus 5% TK100. It lies in the conservative initial acrylic test band and the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% minor-resin cluster, minimizing departure from the characterized reactive chemistry without sacrificing discrimination.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: The experiment card is retained, but the proposed interpretation is narrowed. Treat the 120 C and 130 C values as direct candidate-specific measurements and E_eta only as an apparent rheological descriptor. Do not claim 3.40%-resolution hypothesis acceptance or falsification against the unmodified core from the single-preparation protocol. Chemistry support is adequate for this direct sweep, but it does not establish unrestricted shared-shape transfer for later M-ANCHOR use.
residual_decision_risk: A single preparation does not quantify the large realization/process-state variability observed for E2.
The card lacks a contemporaneous unmodified E2 comparator under matched preparation, elapsed-time, and measurement histories.
The 3.40% shared-shape fit residual does not represent between-preparation discrimination resolution.
Changing AC1920 and TK100 together prevents modifier-specific attribution without single-axis controls.
Modifier reactive functionality and any resulting NCO:OH change have not been verified.
Thermal-hold drift remains unresolved because M-SWEEP measures temperature response rather than residence-time stability.
The five-way tie is broken by minimum modifier burden rather than a scored VOI distinction; all tied cards share the same reference and process-state limitations.
The perturbation analysis covers only individual weight scalings from 0.5 to 1.5; joint or more extreme re-weightings were not evaluated.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not identify a better selectable card and explicitly recommends retaining S1C41::M-SWEEP. However, the card as written uses one S1C41 preparation and lacks a contemporaneous matched-state E2 comparator, while historical E2 realization spread is 2.80-3.57-fold. Therefore the 3.40% curve-fit residual is not a defensible experimental resolution for the claimed relative formulation-level test. The sweep can still directly establish S1C41 viscosity at 120 and 130 C and its candidate-specific temperature response, but its result cannot by itself support the proposed percentage-change classification or robustly falsify the three formulation-level hypotheses. That interpretation would require matched independent S1C41 and E2 preparations and an uncertainty threshold derived from their preparation-level contrasts. The tied alternatives have the same measurement plan and process-state limitation, so the objection does not favor another member of the tied set.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C41::M-SWEEP remains in the unchanged five-card tied top set under every reported one-term scaling from 0.5 to 1.5. All recommendation_flip_boundary entries are null, top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, and no flipped scenarios were observed. The base margin to the first strictly lower card is 0.002292. Thus no weighting tested in the supplied sweep changes the decision; weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated and cannot be adjudicated from this report.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The directly measured 80-130 C M-SWEEP remains inside the empirical support generated for S1C41 itself and does not transfer the unmodified-family thermal shape into the AC1920/TK100 chemistry. This part of the proposal survives. Any later M-ANCHOR use for this chemistry would require a versioned direct sweep demonstrating shape transferability; the present sweep can provide that verification, but only for the chemistry and state range actually measured.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: Although a single sweep can return absolute viscosities at 120 and 130 C, the stated criteria require a percentage change against an unmodified reactive-core reference that the protocol does not measure under matched preparation and elapsed-time conditions. Historical E2 values cannot supply a 3.40%-resolution denominator because their observed spread is approximately 2.8-3.6-fold. Thus the specified protocol cannot defensibly meet the stated falsification criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A single realization could be classified as dilution, elevation, or depression because of preparation state rather than the registered formulation-level rule, so the claim that all three hypotheses were experimentally separated would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The numerical predictions for S1C41 are widely separated (-42.76%, 17.24%, and -72.76%, versus a declared 3.40% threshold), but the protocol specifies only one freshly prepared S1C41 sample and M-SWEEP has min_repeats = 1. The supplied E2 data show 2.80-3.57-fold between-preparation spread, including a 3.57 max/min ratio and 0.585 CV at 120 C. Therefore the 3.40% shared-shape fit residual is not the experimental resolution for a formulation-level comparison across preparations. The hypotheses remain entangled with realization/process state despite proposer.hypotheses_not_separated being empty.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could compare S1C41 with the declared numerical formulation-level predictions, but it could not support modifier-specific association, joint plasticization, or inert-dilution mechanism attribution.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: 15.0% AC1920 and 5.0% TK100 are introduced while the E2 reactive core is reduced to 80.0%. With no acrylic-only or tackifier-only control, an elevation above -42.76% cannot be attributed specifically to the acrylic-like axis, and a depression below -42.76% cannot establish that both modifiers form a plasticizing continuum or determine which modifier caused it. In addition, the supplied E2 note requires recalculation of NCO:OH if either modifier has reactive functionality, but no verified modifier functionality or recalculated stoichiometry is included.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The reported relative change could depend on an arbitrary or unmatched E2 reference and an unspecified temperature aggregation rather than being a directly observed matched-state quantity.
objections.objection: The candidate viscosity at 120 and 130 C is read directly, which is a strength, but the claimed primary result is a percentage level change relative to the unmodified reactive core. The M-SWEEP protocol only says to sweep one freshly prepared S1C41 sample and does not include a contemporaneous, matched-state unmodified E2 comparator or specify which historical E2 realization supplies the denominator. It also does not specify whether the 120 and 130 C relative changes are classified separately or combined into one '120-130 C level change.' The accompanying E_eta descriptor additionally requires regression of ln(eta) against 1/T, although it is secondary to the direct level measurements.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary level claim is undermined on this ground, provided the 120 and 130 C values remain direct measurements and the fitted E_eta is treated only as a candidate-specific rheological descriptor.
objections.objection: This attack surface is adequately handled. S1C41 is explicitly identified as resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 and outside the validated unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared-shape support. The selected M-SWEEP directly measures 80-130 C and does not reconstruct 120-130 C values from the unmodified-family shape. The proposal therefore does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape outside its measured support.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The protocol cannot produce a defensible matched-reference result satisfying the preregistered falsification criteria; any formal falsification would depend on an unstated baseline and would understate realization uncertainty.
objections.objection: The stated falsification rules require a measured percentage change relative to the unmodified core, but the protocol contains no matched unmodified-core measurement and no rule for choosing among the historically variable E2 realizations. Moreover, the 3.40% value comes from a shared-shape-plus-intercept fit residual, not from between-preparation repeatability, while the protocol permits one preparation. The association and plasticization criteria also use the exact -42.76% boundary without an uncertainty band, even though experimental variation around that boundary is much larger than 3.40%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Overstating E_eta as molecular evidence or representing the later grid as a contemporaneously frozen design would exceed the evidence, although no actual hidden-outcome dependence is established by the payload.
objections.objection: No direct use of an unmeasured S1C41 outcome is shown, and the proposer appropriately limits interpretation to formulation-level rules rather than claiming a molecular mechanism. The fitted E_eta must continue to be described only as an apparent rheological temperature-response descriptor, not a chemical reaction activation energy. The payload notes that the current exact grid and refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no contemporaneous repository freeze artifact is available, but it also explicitly states that validation coordinates and outcomes were excluded; this is a provenance limitation rather than demonstrated outcome leakage.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain S1C41::M-SWEEP but run at least three independent, fully recorded S1C41 preparations together with at least three contemporaneous unmodified E2-core preparations under matched preparation, elapsed-time, and measurement histories. Predefine separate 120 C and 130 C relative-change calculations and base the classification threshold on the observed uncertainty of those matched preparation-level contrasts rather than the 3.40% curve-fit residual. If modifier-specific attribution is intended, also add matched M-SWEEP single-axis controls at 15% AC1920 only and 5% TK100 only; otherwise explicitly restrict the conclusion to the combined S1C41 formulation.
skeptic.strongest_objection: M-SWEEP permits only one S1C41 preparation and includes no contemporaneous matched-state unmodified E2 comparator, even though the claimed observable is a relative level change and E2 shows 2.80-3.57-fold realization spread. Consequently, the 3.40% fit residual cannot serve as the experimental discrimination resolution for the proposed formulation-level test.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking. It is needed to establish the chemistry provenance, state-shift evidence, one-point calibration error, shared thermal-response support, and original hold contrast.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
